result.title: GRADUS: Discovering and Recovering Agent Lessons from the Environment's Latent Syllabus
result.summary: Training LLM agents for policy-constrained tool environments, such as an airline backend with booking, refund, and cancellation policies, requires tasks that exercise the environment's rules individually and in combination. Existing synthesis pipelines let a model propose tasks and retain only those it immediately solves, biasing training data toward easier behaviors. We introduce Gradus (Graded Rungs of Ascending Difficulty from an Underlying System), which decouples what a task should teach from the concrete task and solution used to teach it. Without seed tasks, Gradus treats a fixed environment as a latent syllabus, extracting guarded behavioral operators that capture how actions depend on current conditions and how their effects reshape subsequent decisions. It composes these operators into increasingly demanding tasks while using corpus-level feedback to target missing outcome combinations. Crucially, Gradus jointly calibrates tasks and solutions against the environment: execution feedback identifies which side to refine while preserving the intended behavioral requirements. Verification thus becomes a recovery signal rather than a terminal filter, coupling coverage-guided exploration with the preservation of difficult examples. From off-the-shelf backbones, the resulting curriculum lifts a 30B model from 59% to 89% on $τ^2$-Bench and from 47% to 83% on CAR-Bench with an Opus 4.5 proposer, and to 76% and 62%, respectively, with an open-weight Qwen3-235B proposer. These results show the value of jointly controlling which behaviors are explored and which survive into verified training data.

AI.brief_summary: Gradus 将固定的工具环境视为潜在课程表，从中抽取带条件约束的行为算子并组合成递进任务，再用语料级反馈补齐缺失的结果组合，同时联合校准任务与解法，把执行验证当作修复信号而非终端过滤，从而提升 agent 在 τ²-Bench 和 CAR-Bench 上的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本 agent 任务合成，与视觉推理无直接关系；但「验证作为恢复信号而非过滤」和覆盖导向的轨迹构造，可供核查 LVR 轨迹训练中哪些样本与行为组合能进入监督，以及任务难度与解法的联合校准如何影响贡献分配。
